title: Quality finding
description:
One thing about a build that falls short of a bar, stated as work a specialist can do.

Every producer that judges a build - playability, production-quality, visual-qa, review, verification, listing-validation, a person at G4, and later the quality scorecard - reports its failures in its own shape. A quality finding is the one shape they are all normalized into, so that a finding can be routed to the discipline that owns it without a person translating it: the quality dimension it concerns, how severe it is, what was measured against which bar, the evidence, the owner discipline (a role in core/roles/roles.yaml), the concrete task (what to change, and how a re-measurement accepts it) and the route that takes it there (core/reference/specialist-routing.yaml).

A finding's `id` is stable across measurements of the same check by the same producer, which is what lets the gate that raised it say on the next build whether it was resolved.

`request` is what a person types at G4 (`wgf decide <run> iterate --findings FILE`): the dimension, severity, summary and task. The owner and the route are filled from the routing data, never guessed by the person.

dimension.description: The quality dimension a finding concerns. Each is owned by exactly one specialist (core/reference/specialist-routing.yaml `specialists`).

severity.description: blocker: the producer failed the build on it. major: a defect the producer saw that did not fail the build on its own. minor: polish.

route.description: Where the work is done: the game's code and content (develop, as the owning specialist), an asset made again (assets), the design revised - a scope or content increase the design must state first (design), or the store listing (listing).

change.description: What to change, in the build's terms.

acceptance.description: How the change is accepted: what the producer that raised the finding re-measures on the next build, or what the person who raised it checks at G4.

design_field.description: The game-design field a design-route finding concerns (e.g. build_spec.content).

producer.description: The artifact type the finding was read from (playability-report, production-quality-report, visual-qa-report, review-report, qa-report, listing-validation-report, decision-record), or `quality-scorecard`.

step.description: The workflow step that produced it.

check.description: The producer's own id for what failed: a check id, a VQA failed id (score:environment), a blocker id, a defect id.

project.description: The viewport (desktop, mobile) it was measured on, when the producer says.

request.description: A finding as a person states it at G4.

route.description: A person may ask for `design` (a scope or content increase the design must state first) or `assets` (an asset made again); otherwise the routing data decides.

measured.description: What the producer measured, as it reported it.

bar.description: The bar it was measured against, as the producer stated it.

evidence_refs.description: Frames, files and artifacts that show it: run-relative or absolute frame paths, repository paths, artifact ids.

owner.description: The specialist role (core/roles/roles.yaml) that owns the finding's dimension.

assets.description: Asset ids it concerns, when the producer names them.

build.description: The build a finding was measured on: its commit, and the digest of its bundle when verification built it (verification-report build_artifact.content_hash), else null.

status.description: A finding's lifecycle. detected: a producer reported it. classified: its dimension, owner and route were decided from the routing data. assigned: a triage routed it to its owner. implemented: the owner's visit built a change for it. verified: the producer that raised it re-measured a newer build and it no longer fails, and nothing that was passing failed on that build (a fix that regresses another gate is not verified). closed: verified, and every gate the run holds a report of has measured the build carrying the fix. Never closed on the specialist's word: only on the raising gate's re-measurement. A verified or closed finding the gate raises again is classified again (reopened).

record.description: A finding in the run's lifecycle ledger (triage-report `lifecycle`): the finding as last measured, its status, every transition, and the verification evidence.

build.description: The build it was last observed failing on (the affected build).

expected.description: The threshold it is held to (the finding's bar).

observed.description: The value last measured (the finding's measured).

fix.description: The specialist visit that implemented it.

verification.description: The raising producer's re-measurement of a newer build than the fix: its report, the build, what it measured, and any regressions that keep the finding from being verified.

regressions.description: Findings first detected on a build at or after the fix: something that was passing fails now.

gates_measured.description: The producers whose reports measured a build at or after the fix.

detected_seq.description: Run-local order of the report it was first detected in.

by.description: The artifact or step the transition came from.
